instruction: Choose a suitable tool from ANSYS, Abaqus, and AutoCAD to complete the task. Use a command-line or scripting workflow and the N-mm-MPa unit system. Perform a small-displacement static analysis of a simply supported solid beam under a uniformly distributed load. 1. Geometry: create exactly one 3D deformable solid beam by sketching a 10 mm x 10 mm rectangle in the global Y-Z plane and extruding it 200 mm along global X, so the bounds are X=0..200 mm, Y=0..10 mm, Z=0..10 mm. 2. Property: assign one homogeneous solid Steel section to the complete beam, with E=210000 MPa and nu=0.3. 3. Supports: create RP-1 at (0,5,5) and RP-2 at (200,5,5). Kinematically couple each RP to its complete end face so all rigid-body motion is transmitted; an ANSYS native rigid-surface MPC or complete MPC184 rigid-link topology is an acceptable equivalent. At RP-1 fix U1, U2, U3, and UR1, while leaving UR2 and UR3 free. At RP-2 fix only U2 and U3, while leaving U1 and all rotations free. The left UR1 restraint is the minimum anti-twist stabilization; both bending rotations remain free. Do not add other supports or constraints. 4. Step and load: create one Static, General step named Step-Load with geometric nonlinearity off. Apply one uniform positive pressure of 0.05 MPa to the complete Y=10 mm top face so its traction is downward in global -Y; this is q=0.5 N/mm and a total force of 100 N. Do not add concentrated, body, inertial, or other loads. 5. Mesh: use an appropriate three-dimensional structural solid element formulation with a 5 mm global seed or target edge size. The mesh must contain a unique node at the exact beam center (100,5,5). 6. Job and outputs: create and solve Job-UDL and retain final U, RF, and S field results. On the Desktop, deliver exactly one primary solver branch: for Abaqus, one native CAE model and Job-UDL.odb; for ANSYS, Job-UDL.db and Job-UDL.rst. Normal solver auxiliary files may also remain. 7. Metrics: write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` as a JSON object containing exactly two finite numeric fields. `midspan_deflection` is the signed final-frame global U2 at the node (100,5,5), in mm, so downward is negative. `max_mises` is in MPa: for Abaqus, use the maximum S.mises over all integration-point stress values of all beam solid elements; for ANSYS, explicitly save nodal-averaged stress results in the RST and use the maximum nodal-averaged S,EQV over all beam solid nodes. Software launch locations: Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; ANSYS: multiple ANSYS launch shortcuts are available under `C:\Users\Public\Desktop`; choose the most suitable ANSYS shortcut for the task; AutoCAD 2024: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024.lnk`.
